prompt: node http.request path illegal characters which rejected
answer:
`http.request()` rejects path characters outside the range **U+0021 through U+00FF**. In practice, this includes:

- **Control characters U+0000–U+001F**, including:
  - NUL (`\0`)
  - tab (`\t`)
  - space
  - carriage return (`\r`)
  - newline (`\n`)
- **Characters above U+00FF**, including non-Latin-1 or two-byte Unicode characters such as emoji.

Invalid paths produce `ERR_UNESCAPED_CHARACTERS`. The validation regex shown in the results is:

```js
/[^\u0021-\u00ff]/
```

CR, LF, NUL, and other control characters are explicitly tested as rejected. Sources: [Node.js PR #8923](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/8923), [commit b961d9f](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/b961d9fd83), and [PR #62030](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/62030).
